tool.name: Trackastra CTC export
tool.description: prepare tracked masks and lineage data for Napari and external CTC tools
tool.command: mkdir -p 'ctc_masks' && #for $i, $mask in enumerate($tracked_masks): #set $frame = '%04d' % $i ln -s '$mask' 'ctc_masks/man_track${frame}.tiff' && #end for python '$__tool_directory__/ctc_to_napari.py' --track-table '$track_table' --masks-dir 'ctc_masks' --tracks-out 'napari_tracks.tabular' --graph-out 'napari_graph.json' --stack-out 'napari_tracked_stack.tiff' --ctc-dir 'ctc_output'

param.name: track_table
param.label: CTC track table
param.help: The Trackastra man_track.txt output containing track ID, start frame, end frame, and parent track ID.

param.name: tracked_masks
param.label: Tracked CTC masks
param.help: Ordered Trackastra mask collection. Collection order defines time and must begin at frame 0.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Converts the Cell Tracking Challenge outputs of Trackastra into a form that the Napari interactive tool can open, and into files that other Cell Tracking Challenge software can read.
**Inputs**
The ``man_track.txt`` track table and the tracked mask collection from the same Trackastra run.
**Outputs**
* Napari image stack: the tracked masks as one multi-page TIFF with time as the leading axis. The tracks table and the lineage graph are stored in the TIFF description. * Napari tracks: columns track_id, t, y, x for 2D data and track_id, t, z, y, x for 3D data, sorted by track and time. * Napari lineage graph: JSON mapping each child track ID to its parent track ID. * CTC masks: the masks under ``man_trackNNNN`` element identifiers. Downloading the collection next to the track table gives a Cell Tracking Challenge directory.
**Viewing in Napari**
The Napari interactive tool accepts image datasets only, so select the Napari image stack. It opens as one layer with a time slider. To add the lineage as a Tracks layer, run this in the Napari console::
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np import tifffile
with tifffile.TiffFile(next(Path.home().glob("input/*.tif*"))) as handle: masks = handle.asarray() meta = handle.shaped_metadata[0]["trackastra"]
graph = {int(child): [int(p) for p in parents] for child, parents in meta["napari_graph"].items()} viewer.add_labels(masks, name="CTC masks") viewer.add_tracks(np.asarray(meta["napari_tracks"]), graph=graph, name="lineage")
Napari reads CSV files only as Points or Shapes layers, so the tracks table cannot be opened by drag and drop.
